2.0.s.en: (1) The sanctification of the seventh day

2.0.0.en: At the end of the sixth day God completed the creation of the world in its two parts, heaven and earth, and all the host of them, that is, the creatures in them, whether the angels in heaven or man and the animals on the earth. The angels, men and all creatures are God's soldiers, belonging to Him in His army and obeying His laws.

2.1.0.en: The seventh day: the Sabbath day.

2.1.1.en: God rested: He rested in the rest of His creation, that is, He was pleased and rejoiced in the creatures He had made. But this does not mean that He grew weary of creating or that He rested in the sense of not working, for He still works, as He said, "My Father worketh hitherto, and I work" (Jn 5:17). God completed the works of creation in the six days and rejoiced and was pleased with what He had made, and this is His rest.

2.2.0.en: God blessed this day and sanctified it, that is, He made it an opportunity for man for spiritual rest, so that he would set it apart for the worship of God and His service and for fulfilling His will by keeping His commandments. It is noted that the seventh day did not end with an evening and a morning, because it extends until now, for God rejoices in what He has made and in the submission of His children to Him. Many years later the Ten Commandments mentioned the Sabbath day, which is to be sanctified for the worship of God, but it was known before, from the beginning of creation. The Church until now still regards the Sabbath as special, so there is no absolute fasting on it and no prostrations (metanoias) are made on it, but the glory of Sunday surpassed the glory of the Sabbath through the Resurrection of Christ on it, after He died for mankind and redeemed it.

2.2.1.en: Take care of the Lord's Day every week, which is Sunday, so that you spend longer times with God in His worship and service, and you make those around you happy, and God rejoices in you and blesses you.

2.3.0.en: Here he repeats the details of some of the events of the creation of the heavens and the earth, mentioning details of what He created on the third day and showing that there was no rain on the third day, because it arose from the effect of the sun's rays on the seas, so that the water evaporated into clouds and afterward became rain; all this happened on the fourth day. Likewise there was no man to care for the plants, because he was created on the sixth day, and the plants had not yet been created.

2.4.0.en: God brought forth a mist from the earth, which is vapor or a flow of water, and made it water the plants He had created on the third day. This mist was either a means that God made for watering the plants on the third day, or it resulted from the effect of the sun's rays on the seas, which produced the clouds and the mist, because the sun was created immediately after the plants, on the fourth day.

2.5.0.en: Here he explains how man was created: he is from the red dust, and therefore was called "Adam", that is, red, so that he would always remember his origin, that he is from the dust. So although he is the head of all creation, he is to be humble before God and with all people, and he even learns from all creation.

2.5.1.en: Man is distinguished by the breath of God in him, which made him in His image and likeness. This breath gave him not only to move, breathe and do the works of the animals, but to be distinguished from them by the rational spirit, which is not found in any other creature.

2.6.0.en: Garden: a large walled garden, or a paradise, and its diminutive is a little garden.

2.6.1.en: God prepared for Adam a garden to live in and placed in it all the animals and plants, and he explains that its place was in the east and specifies that it was in Eden. It is not the present city of Aden, and the exact place of the garden of Eden is not known, and it is thought that it was in Iraq.

2.7.0.en: God planted in the garden trees with fruit pleasant to the sight and delicious to the taste; and He also planted in the midst of the garden the tree of life, which gives strength and vigor to man by eating of its fruit, and even gives him the ability to be incorruptible, that is, immortal, as is shown by what He says about it in (ch. 3:22), that if Adam continued to eat of it he would live forever. It is a type of Christ, the Bread of life, who gives us His Body and Blood on the altar in the New Testament. It is also a type of the Cross, which gave us redemption and life.

2.7.1.en: He also caused to grow the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, from which man was forbidden to eat. It was an ordinary tree and there was no sin in it, but the sin was in disobeying God by eating of it.

2.8.0.en: He explains that there was a river that watered the garden and divided into four branches. There are many opinions about the places of these rivers that are mentioned next, but no one can determine their place exactly, even if the names are similar, because these places may have been named after the names of the rivers mentioned in the Book of Genesis.

2.9.0.en: Pison: its meaning is overflowing, or flowing violently.

2.9.1.en: Bdellium: a kind of gum-bearing or medicinal tree, and some thought it a kind of pearl. Onyx: a kind of precious stone.

2.9.2.en: He called the first branch of this river Pison, and it compasses the land called Havilah, in which there are gold mines of a good kind, and in this land there are also bdellium and onyx.

2.10.0.en: The second branch is the river Gihon, and its meaning is bursting forth, and it compasses the land called Ethiopia (Cush).

2.11.0.en: Hiddekel: that is, the Tigris, and its meaning is lightness and swiftness, while the Euphrates means the abundant or the holy.

2.11.1.en: God in His love prepared for you a perfect paradise and distinguished you from the rest of creatures by the human spirit, so thank Him at all times for His gifts, and look at all creation, and it will speak to you of Him, for it is He who made it wonderful. And when you have dominion over the whole world and many praise you, do not forget that you were created from dust, so look at the earth from which you were taken, and bear the offenses of others, and do not despise anyone.

2.12.0.en: God created Adam from the dust (v. 7), then prepared the garden for him (v. 8) and put him in it, and made him a leader and responsible for the whole world, and asked him to care for all the plants and animals, tending the growth of the plants, the trees and their fruits, and guarding them from the animals so that they would not destroy them but only eat of them. Adam worked with joy because he worked with God and for Him and felt His presence with him. This shows the importance of work in the life of the children of God, and that it is a blessing and not a burden, but the distress of work appeared after the Fall, as is made clear by His saying, "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread" (ch. 3:19), that is, the feeling of weariness from work began after the Fall.

2.12.1.en: Take care to have good works in every place you go, and force yourself to work even if only a little, and you will feel confidence in yourself, benefit others, close the door against the wars of the demons, and be able to practice your worship and service with energy and competence and be an example to those around you.

2.13.0.en: God gave the plants and the fruits of the trees as food for man, and when He speaks to Adam He means Adam and Eve, that is, the whole human race. But God gave man a commandment not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, to show His concern for man's freedom and as a test of his obedience and sonship to Him. For despite God's fatherhood and His boundless love toward man, He gave him the freedom to remain with Him and enjoy every grace, or to reject His word and eat of the tree He had forbidden. And as a warning of the gravity of disobeying God and being separated from Him, He told him that if he ate of the tree he would die.

2.13.1.en: Adam had known the meaning of death from the fall of the angels, who had been created before. The commandment is not a restriction of man's freedom but a proof of his love for God and a confirmation of his enjoying freedom beyond the rest of creatures. For what would be the benefit if there were no commandment? He would be compelled to do good as a natural law for him, like the animals, that is, not liable to error.

2.13.2.en: And God in His foreknowledge knows that man will fall into sin and will need redemption, and God accepted this great condescension because of His love for him, for He was not pleased with his destruction. This confirms two things:

2.13.3.en: 1- The surpassing love of God for man.

2.13.4.en: 2- God's insistence on man's enjoying freedom.

2.14.0.en: Adam looked at all the animals moving around him and found them male and female, and he felt the harmony among them and also rejoiced in their company, but they did not rise to the level of understanding with him and did not satisfy his needs. He received everything from God, whose fellowship he enjoyed, but he needed God to give him someone like himself to help him in his life and be in harmony with him, each giving his love to the other. Here God shows Adam's need of a woman to share his life, so that his joy might be complete.

2.15.0.en: God showed Adam's leadership over all creatures, the first of which were the animals, and asked him to name each animal by its name. This means the intelligence and surpassing wisdom that Adam enjoyed, so that he was able to understand the natures of the animals, distinguish between them, divide them into different kinds and name each animal with the name suitable for it. This includes all the animals, large and small, that move on the earth, that fly in the heaven, and that travel in the seas and waters. It is understood implicitly that he also called all the plants by their names after dividing them into different classes, which is what is now studied in the various universities, that is, the science of the classification of plants, animals and insects.

2.15.1.en: It is also understood implicitly that he called all the things on the earth, such as the mountains, hills, valleys, rivers...

2.15.2.en: Man is the head of creation and its leader in glorifying God and praising Him, and of course it is not right for him to become attached to it and be preoccupied with its beauty rather than with God, who gave it to him, as happened in the worship of idols, or as happens now in man's attachment to material things.

2.16.0.en: In order to create a female for Adam, God did not want to create her from the dust, so that she would not be an equal rival to him but a part of him, so that each would feel sympathy toward the other; he loves her because she is part of him, and she loves him because he is her origin and she was taken from him. So God caused Adam to fall into a deep sleep and took one of his ribs and closed up the flesh in its place, or in other words, the wound was healed in its place. God took a rib so that Eve would be from his side and be like him, and not from his head, so that she would be proud toward him, or from his foot, so that he would be proud toward her.

2.16.1.en: And Christ, the Second Adam, slept on the Cross, and the Church came forth from His side when He was pierced with the spear, and His blood flowed to redeem her and give her life, so that she might begin her new life with Him.

2.17.0.en: When Adam awoke from his sleep and saw Eve, he felt that she was from him when he noticed the traces of the rib taken from him, so he said of her that she was a part of his flesh and bones, and he called her woman, that is, the female of man, because she was taken out of man. This gave them feelings of oneness in the bond and completeness between them. This first marriage declares to mankind that every marriage God wanted to be a union between man and woman, so that neither lives without the other, and no differences in character or conduct separate them, but they strive for one life in which each completes the other.

2.18.0.en: Adam prophesied about the human race that every man will leave his father and his mother, between whom he was raised, and be united to the girl he has chosen, and the two shall be one flesh, that is, be united. This is what Christianity completed when it made marriage a holy sacrament in which the Holy Spirit descends to give the couple the ability for the marital union. This verse applies to Christ, who left His Father by the Incarnation without being separated from Him, but appeared in the form of humility, and left His mother, that is, the synagogue of the Jews, and was united to His Church through His Incarnation and redemption, that is, He raised the humanity that believes in Him to the level of union with Him through the Church.

2.19.0.en: Adam and Eve were in innocence before the Fall into sin, so they were not ashamed of their nakedness, but after the Fall they felt the shame of sin and needed clothing. Here God made for them coats of skins, which He obtained from the slaughter of an animal, and they are a type of redemption by the blood of Christ, which clothes them and frees them from the shame of sin.

2.19.1.en: Do not be preoccupied with clothes and outward appearances, for they entered the world to cover the shame of sin, but now that you are clothed with the garments of righteousness in Christ, you need only clothing, merely simple garments that cover you, because righteousness has clothed you first. So do not compare yourself with those around you and seek after passing material things, for you are the son of the King of kings and grace covers you, and indeed you are the greatest of His creatures.

3.0.0.en: Satan entered into the serpent, so it had more intelligence and wisdom than all the animals God had created. All the animals have no mind and no ability to speak, but the serpent, by the Satan who had entered it, was able to draw man into sin by evil wisdom. It appears that man noticed this wisdom and did not reject it but may even have admired it, so he accepted to talk with the serpent, although he lived with God in spiritual fullness and did not need another wisdom or intelligence from any other creature, and here is the beginning of the Fall, that is, accepting understanding apart from God and admiring worldly wisdom. It is noted that the serpent went to Eve and not to Adam because Eve is distinguished by emotion, so she could be won over to sin through her emotions; moreover, Eve is Adam's helper and companion, the creature nearest to him, and she could influence him, so although his mind might reject the words of the serpent, his relationship with his wife and his sympathy with her helped his fall into sin. The serpent's question to Eve provoked her against God and was false at the same time, for it said to her as if it were a question, but what was meant was to provoke her to become vexed with God, so it said, "Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?", in order to draw her into dialogue with it, so that it could win her over and make her fall into sin.

3.1.0.en: The woman denied the serpent's words and declared that God had not forbidden them to eat of all the trees of the garden, then she accepted dialogue with Satan dwelling in the serpent and said that God had forbidden them only to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil planted in the midst of the garden, and she fell into the sin of exaggeration, saying that God had said to them not to touch this tree nor its fruit, although God had not said this, and she declared the punishment for eating of the tree, which is death.

3.2.0.en: The evil of Satan dwelling in the serpent appeared when he ascribed falsehood to God and offered the woman a false comfort and a lying promise that they would not die if they ate of the tree. Yet the woman did not take heed and withdraw from this evil dialogue with the serpent.

3.3.0.en: Satan continued in his lie, ascribing cruelty and selfishness to God in depriving man of knowledge and greatness, for by his deceit he presented the knowledge of good and evil as something great that would make them equal to God, although they already knew the good, while evil is not an addition but a deprivation and the opposite of good, as darkness is the opposite of light. So Satan presented the knowledge of evil as something attractive and drew the woman's heart to it, and by accepting Satan's words the woman and Adam fell into pride, the pursuit of a strange knowledge apart from God, and submission to Satan's guidance, and these are some aspects of the first sin into which man fell.

3.4.0.en: By Satan's words desire was stirred in Eve's heart, so she saw the tree and its forbidden fruit as beautiful, appetizing and pleasing, although she had not seen it so before, and this was because she accepted dialogue with Satan. The woman yielded to his seduction, so she put out her hand and ate of the tree, and by this she was separated from God by disobedience and fell into evil. And when she fell, her feelings were defiled, so she wanted to make her husband fall into evil too, and she was no longer a helper to him but a means of making him fall into sin. As for Adam, he loved his wife more than God, so that he accepted her word and rejected God's commandment, and fell into sin.

3.5.0.en: The eyes of Adam and Eve were opened to evil and they lost their first purity, so they felt their nakedness and shame and tried to cover their shame with leaves. They took fig leaves and tried to join them to one another, that is, to sew them, to cover their nakedness, and of course these leaves would dry and fall off easily and would not cover them. These are human attempts to heal the shame of sin, which are of no avail, but God's tenderness would cover them with coats of skins, as we shall see in (v. 21).

3.5.1.en: Do not accept dialogue with Satan in the form of thoughts that disturb you to no purpose and even lead to your withdrawal from God, for these are the marks of Satan's thoughts, whereas God's thoughts are constructive and restful to the soul. And do not give Satan an opportunity through free time, to enter you through it, and keep away from stumbling media or conversation with bad friends, and occupy yourself with God and with every good work you choose for your benefit, and you will keep your purity at all times.

3.6.0.en: Although Adam had lost much of his understanding after the Fall, because of his close relationship with God he still knew the sound of His footsteps, and no one can know the sound of another's footsteps unless he has had a strong relationship with him for a long time, so this confirms the fellowship and the strong relationship between him and God. This time, unlike all the previous times, he did not hasten to meet God, whom he loved and always longed to see, but fled because of his sin, which had separated him from God, and in his great ignorance he hid among the trees, forgetting that God sees everything everywhere and that the trees do not hide anything from His sight.

3.6.1.en: And it says "in the cool of the day", that is, at the blowing of the wind of the day, which is a type of the Holy Spirit, for wind and spirit come as renderings of one word, so God draws near to man to fill him and satisfy him with His Holy Spirit. The voice means the Word of God, who calls man and seeks his salvation. When man sinned he did not go to God but sank into his shame and embarrassment, so the love of God appeared, who took the initiative toward him to seek his salvation, for the strong goes to the weak to support him (Rom 15:1), and sin is a weakness that pains and shames the one who commits it, so he keeps away from apology and needs someone to help him and raise him up in love from his sin.

3.6.2.en: Would that you feel the weakness of those who sin against you and forget yourself, your dignity and your love of possessions, so that you pray for them and even go to them in love to rebuke them, restore the relationship with them, forgive them for what they did and give up what they seized from you, to be like God your Father, who comes to you in His love to raise you from your falls and urge you to repentance, so you experience fellowship with Him and win all those around you.

3.7.0.en: God knows and sees Adam in his hiding place, but He calls him to invite him to repentance and to the confession of his sin, and had he done this, Christ would have become incarnate and redeemed him at that time.

3.8.0.en: Adam declared the reason for his fleeing from God, which was the shame of sin that he felt after the Fall, that is, his feeling of nakedness, and his answer shows his understanding that God knows his place but is calling him to repentance and confession, but unfortunately he did not do so because of his absorption in the feelings of sin, that is, fear and shame.

3.8.1.en: When you sin, do not sink into feelings of grief because of your fall, but know that God loves you and calls you to return to Him. So hasten to repentance and ask His help to make up for what you lost because of the fall and to resist the devil so that he flees from you.

3.9.0.en: When God saw man in his shame, unable to acknowledge his sin, He helped him and encouraged him to repent by asking him, "Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?" For the compassionate God not only accepts the repentance of the sinner but encourages him to it and is patient with him.

3.10.0.en: Unfortunately Adam did not confess his sin, but on the contrary ascribed the fault to Eve and justified himself, and by this he also ascribes the fault to God, because it was He who created Eve for him.

3.11.0.en: Likewise the woman did not confess her sin but ascribed the sin to the serpent that deceived her, and by this she also ascribes the fault to God, who created the serpent.

3.12.0.en: God first decreed the punishment of the serpent, and what is meant more is Satan, who worked in it, which is why Satan is called the old serpent, and the punishment was:

3.12.1.en: 1- The divine curse, that is, the loss of every blessing and exposure to many troubles.

3.12.2.en: 2- The loss of its beautiful appearance, for it appears that the serpent was upright at first, but when God cursed it, it came to crawl on its belly.

3.12.3.en: 3- It came to cleave to the dust of the earth, which enters its mouth instead of food. It is a type of every wicked person who is bound to evil desires, so that his level declines and he returns to the dust from which he was taken, having lost the loftiness of the spirit that God gave him.

3.12.4.en: 4- The existence of continual enmity between the serpent and man, so the snakes seek to bite man on his feet, which are near them because they crawl on the ground, while he treads on its head to crush it and kill it. The serpent, as we mentioned, is a type of Satan, who tries to bite man with his evil desires, but man by the grace of God is able to crush all his power and overcome him.

3.12.5.en: The seed of the woman who bruises the serpent's head is Christ, who crushes Satan and binds him on the Cross and frees His children who believe in Him from his grip and transfers them to Paradise.

3.13.0.en: As for the punishment of the woman, no mention of a curse came in it, because she, with Adam, is the image of God, so she is not cursed, and she would be redeemed by Christ in the fullness of time. This punishment included two things:

3.13.1.en: 1- The pains of childbirth, that is, there is no life or existence for the woman's offspring except through pain. The pains of childbirth are found only in human beings, while the animals do not suffer pains during birth, so that the woman, throughout her generations, would remember her sin and repent and guard against the wars of the devil, for whenever she shares with God in creation and in giving life to a newborn, she remembers the death into which she fell because of her sin and repents.

3.13.2.en: 2- The corruption of the relationship between man and woman, for Adam at first longed for her and she responded to him with longings of love, but after the Fall she longs for him with many emotions, while he inclines to lordship and domination. She longs for him to do her will and he dominates her to do his will, and by this they lost the spirit of oneness and love, which would return to them in Christ the Redeemer through the sacrament of marriage and the work of the Holy Spirit in them. Therefore the inclination of either party to dominate the other, whether the woman by her wiles or the man by his control, is a return to the state of sin and its evil results.

3.14.0.en: God created the earth for man and blessed it to give him fruit to eat, but when man fell the earth was cursed because of him and lost the blessing, so it no longer gave him rich fruit as it had before but dry plants whose leaves turned into thorns that hurt him.

3.14.1.en: It is noted that God did not curse Adam, because, as we said, he is His image, but He cursed the earth, so that when man finds that it does not give him the fruit he wants, this leads him to repentance and to seeking spiritual fruits instead of the fruits of the earth. It is noted that Adam's punishment was the following:

3.14.2.en: 1- The cursing of the earth because of him, so that dry plants that hurt him spread in it, such as thorns and thistles. Thistles: a thorny plant whose fruit is rough.

3.14.3.en: It is noted that Christ bore the crown of thorns on His head, that is, the punishment of sin, and died on the Cross for the redemption of man, that he might enjoy happiness in the Paradise of bliss and the Kingdom of Heaven.

3.14.4.en: 2- Toil in work, for it was no longer pleasant as it was before the Fall, but pain and weariness began, as He said, "In sorrow shalt thou eat of it" (v. 17), "In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread" (v. 19), and this weariness and pain continue throughout man's life.

3.14.5.en: 3- Man dies bodily and is laid in the dust, and his body even decays, for as he was created from the dust, he returns to the dust.

3.14.6.en: If you feel God's presence with you, you will do everything for Him and love work and reject laziness and rejoice in every work you do because you offer it to God, so you experience happiness on earth and then the joys of heaven.

3.15.0.en: After man was driven out of the garden, Adam felt hope in God's promise of salvation, which would come from the seed of the woman, so he called his wife "Eve", that is, the mother of all living, so that from her seed would come Christ the Living One, the Source of life, and give salvation to Adam and his sons who believe in Him.

3.16.0.en: God slaughtered an animal, took its skin and made from it coats, that is, garments, which He put on Adam and Eve, and He taught man the rite of slaughtering an animal and offering it to God, because man had not yet begun to eat meat or animals. The meaning of this is that God taught him how to offer the animal as a burnt offering to Him after seeing its blood shed, so that he might learn that without the shedding of blood God is not pleased with him, nor does it cover his shame, nor does He forgive his sins. Man's attempt to cover himself with fig leaves did not avail, because they would dry and fall off, but by God's work, by the shedding of the blood of the animal, which is a type of the blood of Christ, man obtained coats of skins that last with him.

3.17.0.en: Adam knew the good, but when he ate of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, the knowledge of evil was added to him, and his nature became corrupt and inclined to doing evil. So God in His care wanted to protect him from continuing in evil and being immortal in it, lest he live separated from God and perish, so it was necessary to drive him out of the garden in which he had refused to live with God by eating of the tree, and lest he eat of the tree of life, which gives immortality, and so be immortal in evil.

3.18.0.en: Adam used to work in the garden, but after his expulsion he lived with his corrupt nature, inclined to earthly desires, so his direction became toward the earth from which he was taken and not toward God, who breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and he was a lover of bodily things, keeping away from spiritual things to a great extent.

3.19.0.en: After God clothed man with the coats of skins and taught him how to pray by offering burnt offerings, He drove him out of the garden and placed at its gate angels of the order of the Cherubim, which signifies divine justice, and in the hand of these angels was a flaming sword which turned every way, signifying the Word of God, which cuts off all evil from man. The fire declares that our God is a consuming fire who consumes every sin in man and purifies him, and thus man dies in the hope of salvation, and Christ, after His redemption, brings him in and returns him to Paradise, but with a new nature after clothing him with righteousness.

3.19.1.en: How beautiful is Your love for me, O God, that even while I am fallen You seek to return me to Your embrace and teach me the way of repentance and prayer and holding fast to Your redeeming blood, that I may be rid of all evil in me, and You establish Your fear before my eyes, that I may reject evil with Your help, longing for the pure life in Your hands.

3.19.2.en: We note that Adam is a type of Christ in the following:

3.19.3.en: 1- Adam is the beginning of the human race, and Christ is the beginning of the new man after the human race became corrupt.

3.19.4.en: 2- God cast a deep sleep upon Adam and then took a rib from him and made Eve, and Christ died on the Cross and there came out of His side blood and water, with which He acquired His Church.

3.19.5.en: 3- Adam was united with Eve to become one flesh (Gen 2:24), and in Christ divinity and humanity were united, and likewise He is united with the souls of those who believe in Him.

3.19.6.en: 4- Adam was the head of all creation, to govern it and order it to glorify God, and Christ reigns over all the believers to lead them in the praise of God.

3.19.7.en: 5- Adam named the animals by their names, and Christ the Good Shepherd calls His sheep by their names. Abel and Cain
